passages.note: Near-unanimous House vote (0 No) on a bill that creates civil liability for creators/publishers of digital impersonations, not a platform duty.
Prime sponsor of a bill creating a civil cause of action against creators/publishers of digital impersonations, a dimension the ladder's platform/government-duty rungs do not order.

passages.provision_quote: A provider of an interactive computer service may not be subject to an action for DIGITAL IMPERSONATION for PUBLISHING INFORMATION that is provided by another information content provider.
passages.note: The bill text expressly exempts platforms (interactive computer service providers) from liability, confirming the duty falls on the impersonation's creator/publisher, not the platform.

rows.reasoning: Kolodin prime-sponsored and voted Yes on HB 2394 (2024), which creates a civil cause of action for a person harmed by a deceptive 'digital impersonation,' but its own text provides that 'a provider of an interactive computer service may not be subject to an action for digital impersonation for publishing information that is provided by another information content provider,' placing the duty on the impersonation's creator or publisher rather than on platforms. This does not show platforms being made to 'remove false information,' 'label false content,' subject to 'voluntary standards,' protected via 'free speech online and prevent government censorship,' or barred from 'any government involvement in content moderation decisions,' so every passage is adjacent and no chair is established.
